Show HN: Budget – an open-source private budgeting app for Mac and Windows
items.summary: Budget is a free, open-source app for Mac and Windows. With the simple mode, it gives you what you'd expect of a budgeting app: configure budgets and track expenses against those budgets. But, if you're a geek like me and are way too interested in your personal finance, the extended mode offers features like carrying leftover budgets to the next month, splitting expenses across multiple budgets and seeing how much you can freely spend the coming year, while taking into account any large future expenses (like a car insurance where the premium is paid on a yearly basis). This app is the result of a hobby of mine to track my expenses. It started a few years ago in a spreadsheet, but that spreadsheet at some point took me minutes to edit on my MacBook with 8 gigs of RAM. I had the idea to turn it into an app before, but never had the time to do so. I worked in the software industry until halfway through 2024, when LLMs were mostly just used for debugging. But, because of all the positivity I heard about how good they've gotten now, I tried to see if I could turn the spreadsheet into an app with the help of Claude Opus 5.5. I had to point out a couple of bugs and bad decisions (like bad alignment of text and using entire English sentences instead of keywords as keys for translation), but overall, it worked really well. Budgeting apps are of course not new. But, they often are either free but with limited features, free but with an obnoxious amount of cookies and/or ads, free but charge money for important features or charge money to be used at all. The idea of this project is that there are no cookies, no ads, no fees, no data being stored remotely and that the code is open-source. Data ownership stands at the center of the app: you can easily export/import your data and create back-ups (besides the automatic back-ups the app creates for you). It is available to everyone, of course as long as you have a device that is supported (currently only devices that run macOS and Windows). I'm interested to hear if you think this app has any potential and if you think any important features are missing.

items.title: Show HN: Alter – Restyle any website by typing what you want (extension, BYOK)
items.summary: Alter is a Chrome extension: open it on any site, type something like "hide the sidebar and display articles in Hacker News format", or "give text more contrast and add a dark mode," and the change will show up on the site as a live preview. Save it, and it will be there every time you return to the site. Open source and BYOK (currently only Anthropic). It can also do one-off things like downloading the page contents into an MD file, etc. Not on the Chrome Web Store; download the ZIP and use Load unpacked in Developer mode. Would love to hear where it does poorly.
